lines.beat_before: hook: the doll in her glass case on the altar, 1938, short bobbed hair, turned away towards the wall

lines.text: Hokkaido, Japan. Nineteen thirty-eight. A family moving away left a doll at a temple. They called her Okiku.
lines.beat_before: the bell; the years begin to run; candles and offerings change each year

lines.text: The story is that she belonged to a little girl who died young.
Then the priests noticed her hair. It was growing.
lines.beat_before: the bell; her hair is past her chin

lines.text: The temple says it has grown about twenty-five centimetres. When it is trimmed, it grows back.
lines.beat_before: the bell; a trim: scissors and cut hair on the altar for one year; then it is long again

lines.text: Some say it is a child's hair. That has never been shown.
lines.beat_before: the bell; a photograph pinned to the pillar (in it, she faces the camera)

lines.text: Skeptics say old hair can relax and stretch. Or that someone is doing it.
lines.beat_before: the bell; 2000s; her head has turned most of the way

lines.text: Eighty-eight years. Look where she was facing, at the start.
lines.beat_before: the bell; 2020s; she looks over her shoulder at the lens
no bell: the counter stops at the present; silence
